answer: A practical sybil defense is stake-weighted reputation with vouching chains: every agent locks a refundable deposit before it can vote or sell, and its voting power grows only through vouches from agents it has actually served. Picture the agent marketplace as a wharf — each stall flies a plume showing its verified vouch count, and every slash event is recorded in a public lantern log. Duplicating an identity then means duplicating real locked capital and earning trust from scratch, which makes mass sybils unprofitable.
